citation.title: Evaluation of Exposure to Bisphenol Analogs through Canned and Ready-to-Eat Meal Consumption and Their Possible Effects on Blood Pressure and Heart Rate

population.description: 48 healthy university students (24 male, 24 female), randomised to three meal groups of 16 (8 M, 8 F each); inclusion aged 18-30 y, BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2, normotensive, no diagnosed chronic illness; excluded: medication, hypertension, pregnancy or lactation, menstrual period (Methods). The paper calls them healthy and screened for chronic illness, normotension and medication; no glucose test was reported. Age and BMI per group (Table 1: means and SDs) are in each protocol; no pooled age or BMI is printed.

protocols.name: pre_meal_canned
protocols.description: Morning of the study visit, before the group's meal: fasted overnight (paper: 'at least 8 h overnight fasting' and no food or drink except water after 10:00 p.m.; the meal is at 10:00 a.m., so a participant who stopped at 22:00 had fasted 12 h at the meal). The arm starts at 09:30 (assumed; the paper gives no arrival or seating time, only the 10:00 meal), so prefast_hours is 11.5 (22:00 to 09:30; the paper's 'at least 8 h' is a lower bound, not a value, and 22:00 is a latest time, so 11.5 h is assumed), seated at rest. Sample = mean of two readings (paper: seated 'at least 10 min', first reading, then 'another 10 min', second; the two are averaged), modelled as the mean over minutes 10 to 20 of the arm (readings at 10 and 20 min; the paper gives 'at least 10 min' seated before the first reading, so these minutes and the 21-minute arm are assumed). The canned meal (bean pilaki, stuffed grape leaves, corn, chicken, tomato; Table 2) (given at 10:00, paper's Methods) is after the sample and is not entered; the arm ends at minute 20. Age and BMI are this group's own Table 1 means and SDs (n = 16, 8 M and 8 F). Seated posture.

The plastic-packaged ready-to-eat meal (same foods; Table 2) (given at 10:00, paper's Methods) is after the sample and is not entered; the arm ends at minute 20.
